THE TECHNICAL DEFECT
I have had about 5 different laptops (HP Victus, being the best so far, but many other monster laptops too, and a few not so well spec’d laptops too) in the last 7 years 

Many issues with the Legion:
1.	This PC was stuck in dark mode. 6 hours of research, I finally found something called Burn Prevention which is found in Lenovo Vantage, and then hidden away. What this stupid setting does is override Windows setting and enforces dark mode.
2.	PC kept changing Outlook, Word, Excel settings back to default
3.	My Victus, I could connect a 4-in-1 4K USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter Hub 60Hz, Includes USB 3.0 & PD Port to the C Type Port, 2 screens + headphones connected to the Adaptor, then a fourth screen connected to HDMI (that would be PC screen (1), 2 through the adaptor and then a fourth through the HDMI. 
4.	This poor Legion will not allow a set up for 2 extra screens through the adaptor. Originally when purchased, it worked this way. But now, if I do somehow get this set up working, it will work for an hour or 2, but as soon as I open a PDF (for example), the system reverts back to 1 pc screen, and the 2 extra screens are now showing the same display. I then push W+K, go to settings, and screen 3 is not available there. Again, about 6 or 7 hours of reading done on this. I have not found a resolution.
5.	Today, all of a sudden, this laptop will not connect to my printer. All of my other laptops connect, not this one. I was previously connected, but now there are some how 2 drivers for the printer on this laptop, no clue how the second got there, and the printer will not connect, to this laptop only. It just loads the queue.

These are just a few of the issues, but If I can advise anyone wanting to purchase this laptop, I would say stay clear.

6.	Fans are always blasting away.
7.	Temp is always extremely high just below the screen (top of keyboard)
8.	Super slow at start up
9.	Take a second to realise what I am requesting, for example, open excel, it could take about 3 seconds to get the process started. The little men inside are too busy…. Doing nothing, I need to wake them up first.

These technical defects render a brand-new $1,700 premium laptop completely unusable for its intended purpose.

I have a late 2023 Lenovo Legion 5i. Using Lenovo Vantage software it is possible to adjust fan speeds. You click on Thermal Mode in the main screen. That takes you to Performance Mode/Balance Mode/Quiet Mode/Custom Mode. Custom Mode allows you to control the fan speeds for the other three modes, unfortunately you cannot lower the fan speeds, only raise them. 
Fn + Q will also toggle between the Modes. 
Personally I found tweaking fan speeds in Balance Mode and ticking the option to Enable Legion AI Engine dropped my temperatures by almost 15C. It will depend on what games you play. I am not a competitive FPS player and generally play isometric turn based games like Baldurs Gate 3 and Jagged Alliance 3, so the variable cpu clock speeds that this setting gives is not noticeable.

comments.text:
Got my Legion 5 in March 2021. I've been extremely satisfied with it as my daily work and play machine. However, after 2 years of active use and transportation, it has developed some quirks. The first thing to fail was my stock hard drive. After that, keyboard's function row began to die. The Esc key, F4 - F6, and left Alt key have stopped working. My E doesn't always work, either. (Important for gaming!) Since these control the most useful functions, like brightness, and Alt-Tabbing, it's disappointing to have to manually adjust these settings. Also, the LCD screen has suffered some burn-in. The bottom of the screen has permanent vertical streaks staining my view of the taskbar at all times, which itself leaves a slightly permanent shadow of its outline on the display.

I still recommend it, as it has survived more than its fair share of travel (and moisture) over the last 3 years. I think if I can replace the bad keys, I would be happy to keep this machine for another 5 years. For other long term users, I recommend keeping your brightness down a notch, setting your taskbar to Auto-Hide, and picking a short delay for your screen saver! And always make regular backups of your data, no matter what you buy, because you never know! :)

Good luck!

comments.text:
Hi! Last week I just got a used Legion 5 2021 (Ryzen 5 5600H + 3060 115-130W, 8GB RAM, 512GB SSD) for 840 euros and still 1 year warranty remaining (it was initially bought by someone else in early-mid 2022 and sold to a big online retailer in my country, with very little traces of use).
I could have gotten a brand new Ideapad Gaming 3 with 5800H + 90W 3060 directly from Lenovo, or an Acer Nitro 5 also with 5800H + 95W 3060 for the same price, but then I searched for some feedback online and apparently the Ideapad Gaming 3 feels cheap and runs quite hot, and the MUX switch is a deal-breaker for me as I don't want to deal with the iGPU (my previous experience with an AMD iGPU was quite disastrous in the last few months). AMD Laptop GPUs are almost non-existent in my country (7600S was 1500-1900€ which was at the same price point as some 4070 laptops earlier this month, 5500M and 6500M also fell right in the price range of most 3060 laptops) and they weren't compatible with a few things I currently wanted to do until earlier this month. And if you wonder why I didn't get a desktop PC: Simulated on PC Part Picker, a build similar to my laptop in benchmarks would have costed me 50-150 euros more, so slightly outside of my initial budget.

I bought the Legion 5 as my old laptop was starting to be very limiting in modded Minecraft, modded Cities: Skylines (Cities: Skylines 2 is right around the corner too!) and Anno 1800. I'm coming from a now 4 years-old HP Pavilion Gaming Laptop 15-ec0xxx (Ryzen 5 3550H + GTX 1650 50W) which served me quite well all this time.

I was waiting for the 4000 Laptop GPU series benchmarks to decide which laptop to choose, and just saw in another one of your videos the 4050 Laptop GPU was just barely the same as a Max-P 3060 because of its voltage limit and most laptops with a 4050 came with DDR5.
I had already bought a kit of 2x16GB DDR4-3200 CL22 Dual Rank x8 RAM several months ago and got a 1TB Samsung 970 EVO Plus earlier this month as it was getting very cheap.

So far I didn't have any problem with the Legion 5 and I'm very happy about its raw performance! (maybe because my previous laptop was ultimate-bottom tier)
It's surprisingly quiet most of the time, and even pushing the 3060 at 95-100W barely puts it above 70c. The 2 SSDs in the Legion 5 are running so cool they rarely go above 50-55c (even the 970 EVO Plus which is known for running hot).
Battery life is actually surprising: 3 hours, charged at 80%, browsing/watching YT videos and Discord without the iGPU, only using the 3060. I also didn't find the 230W power adapter to not be enough so far.

Overall, I consider it as a pretty good deal, as performance stagnation didn't make the prices drop as fast as expected... Waiting to see how it'll perform in the future! Thank you for your videos!

comments.text:
Jarrod - I have a question in regards to this laptop.  So I bought this laptop (Legion 5, Ryzen 5800H, RTX 3060, 144hz 17" screen) and the problem I have with it is that the spec sheet says the laptop panel itself supports Freesync which means that it support variable refresh rate.  However, as far as I can tell, this is absolutely not true and a complete misrepresentation of the product by Lenovo.  I simply cannot get the laptop panel to enable Freesync at all.  It doesn't matter if I'm in hybrid mode and using the AMD drivers, or in non-hybrid mode and using the NVidia drivers.  Both drivers simply act as though the 17" laptop panel does not have Freesync capabilities.  What I believe is reality is that the laptop display supports EITHER 60Hz or 144Hz, but no in between.

For example, if I play Rocket League on the laptop dispaly and I limit the refresh rate in the in game settings to 120fps, I should still have a very smooth experience if the laptop display support VRR and sync's the Hz to FPS.  However, it is noticeably choppy even though the game is easily locked at 120fps.  If I connect the laptop to my external g-sync monitor and perform the same test, this same 120fps is silky smooth.

I think this is a massive issue with the laptop and should be called out on Lenovo's part as they are straight up lying about their product.  Otherwise, the laptop is fantastic and I love it, but I'm sorely disappointed that they led me to believe the laptop panel supports Freesync when it clearly does not.

The downside to this situation is that unless you can keep your game locked to 144fps then you will have a very choppy and poor experience.  You are almost better off setting the laptop display to 60hz and playing it that way.

So long story short, here's my question.  Does your Legion 5 laptop display support Freesync?  Are you able to enable it in either the AMD drivers or NVidia drivers?  As far as I can tell, this is impossible.

@zsoca31  umm what?
1. 80% is the perfect balance between capacity and longevity. My 11-year old Samsung laptop with the limit of 80% still has like 50-60% of original capacity. It's the last 20% that are the most harmful for the battery. Yes it's optimial to keep the battery charged at 40-50%(not 60), but in case you need to use your laptop suddenly you'd have to spend time to charge it, it's very inconvinient to switch back and forth between 60 and 100% to reach needed capacity. Others offer 60 or 80% choice, heck with Dell you can select the EXACT percentage, ranging from 55 to 100%. 
2. Voltage control is definitely needed in gaming laptops. They often reach 90+ degrees in heavy loads(some heavy games included) and throttle, with undervolting not only you lower temps, you also get more performance back, limited by laptop formfactor.

comments.text: Thanks for the overview of issues with the Legion 5. By no means is this a bad laptop: it's actually still arguably the best Ryzen 5800h+3060 combo machine you can buy (if you CAN buy it). But I actually returned mine for reasons related to some of the issues you mentioned here, such as the lack of fan control. Frankly, I'd also like more control over the CPU speed, but that just doesn't seem possible. The combination of these two omissions produced a gaming experience where the fans would speed up whenever the CPU went over 79 degrees, and then slow down again whenever it went below 80 degrees, which happens frequently enough in my favorite game to make it annoying. Really, I wanted to just either slow down the CPU a little bit, or change the fan curve to ignore temps of up to 82 degrees, but I couldn't do either. The other annoyances I had were the cheap-feeling keys. Yes, I know it's a Lenovo, and they're supposed to have some of the best keyboards, and I use T-series Lenovos at work all the time, and they do have great keyboards. But the one in the current Legion 5 just feels delicate and cheap, like the keys will stop working way before the laptop is obsolete. I think they just keep making the plastic thinner and thinner until there's an issue or something. However, in the end, what compelled me to return it before it was too late was the 6GB video memory. Even at 1080p, that's not quite enough for ultra settings in some games, and I'll be damned if I'm going to turn down the texture quality settings on a brand new, not-cheap gaming laptop because it already comes out of the box with insufficient video RAM. Just one last thing: I didn't have a problem with the 300w power brick, as I frequently see power bricks burn out when they're overspecced (paired with a laptop that requires very nearly the full wattage of the PS). I was actually pleased that the 300w brick was shipped with the 3060 model I had because it means the brick runs much cooler and will likely last as long as the laptop.
